relation_to_FaultTune.task: Accept or reject a fixed pulse update according to the actual target-circuit failure change Delta=p_fail,new-p_fail,old. This is a new explicit Ramsey/pulse-error model family, not a relabeling of the frozen Round4/5 test cases.
relation_to_FaultTune.existing_physical_connection: The existing circuit simulator already uses an unknown coherent Rx phase from H=(omega+u)X/2, explicit commuting phase evolution and Markov dephasing Kraus maps. A known basis change gives the single-qubit Z-phase model here. Repeating a sensing pulse changes both phase and accumulated dephasing; no Bernoulli action probabilities are assigned independently by hand.
relation_to_FaultTune.criteria_retained: Primary cost remains all circuit executions; risks remain1% and eligible correct-decision power95%, with epsilon=.001 from the existing grid. Gate uses and modeled device time are additional paid resource costs. The benchmark files are read only and unchanged.
relation_to_FaultTune.applicability_limit: The contract assumes a known phase axis, a stationary commuting dephasing model, calibrated controllable measurement phases, and a public bounded phase domain. It does not validate the original three-qubit spectator-crosstalk task or arbitrary pulse errors.

physical_model_and_unknown_parameters.primitive: U_phi=exp(-i phi Z/2) is one sensing pulse. Each pulse has the commuting dephasing channel with off-diagonal attenuation exp(-gamma). A fresh Ramsey circuit prepares |+>, appliesk sensing pulses, then measures an arbitrary known equatorial phase.

unknown_domain.bias: a=alpha_0+v/2; it is unknown and is never supplied to a validator

physical_model_and_unknown_parameters.frozen_update: old has phase phi-pi/6, new has phase phi+pi/6 for one target pulse. The known update is delta=pi/3, fixed before validation and independent ofphi. The midpoint pulse U_phi is accessible by the public midpoint control. Known control and analysis phases are the same resource for all methods.
physical_model_and_unknown_parameters.target_probability: p_fail(theta)=a-(v exp(-gamma)/2)cos(theta); hence Delta=(v exp(-gamma)/2)sin(phi). Bias cancels exactly but contrast and dephasing are unknown.
physical_model_and_unknown_parameters.query_probability: At depthk and a chosen quadrature signS in{-1,+1}, Y|S is Bernoulli(a+S*v exp(-gamma*k)sin(k*phi)/2). This follows from the same unitary, dephasing and classical readout channel.
physical_model_and_unknown_parameters.paid_observations: Every delivered Y is a fresh, separately charged circuit outcome. No shared hidden noise, exact simulator probability, truephi/gamma/v, or uncharged calibration data is available.
physical_model_and_unknown_parameters.domain_prior_boundary: The phase interval is a declared parameter-domain assumption, not a data-derived confidence interval. An application lacking this prior must pay to localize phase and handle aliases, with the same information given to every comparator.

resource_contract.actions: All methods may choose any positive integer depthk and any equatorial analysis phase, adaptively between fresh circuits; known commuting phase corrections are allowed. The lower bound even grants arbitrary final single-copy POVMs before the same readout channel.
resource_contract.excluded_new_resources: No cross-circuit quantum memory, entangled multi-probe inputs, coherent noncommuting error-correction controls, or access to a purification of the noise channel. Those would require a different model and new equal-resource baselines.
resource_contract.primary_cost: N=sum1 over all executed circuits, including learning, incorrect decisions and cap abstentions.
resource_contract.gate_cost: G=sumk over those circuits. One unit is one physical sensing-pulse/dephasing period; coherent amplification is never a free query.
resource_contract.device_cost: T=2.2*N+G+0.1*S_switch, following the existing preparation/readout2.2 and configuration-switch0.1 convention. A randomized-quadrature baseline hasT<=sum(k+2.3), whereas every method hasT>=2.2*N+G.
resource_contract.budget: Both explicit baselines use the common finite capN=2^20, already an existing default shot-budget scale. They execute at most16*N sensing pulses. A future comparison must also freeze the allowed depth/menu and any device-time cap; the present information lower bound is stronger in scope because it allows unrestricted depths.
resource_contract.abstention_penalty: The policies only abstain upon exhausting the full shot cap, so actual and full-cap-penalized primary costs agree. No unresolved run is dropped.

strong_comparator_policy.family: Include robust multi-depth Ramsey/phase-estimation and frequency-learning methods with identical depths, nuisance model and risk guarantee. For the impossibility result it suffices to exhibit the two valid fixed-depth controls below: the strongest qualifying comparator is never more expensive than either one.
strong_comparator_policy.no_straw_man: A plain depth1 A/B control is not the strongest same-resource comparator after powersU^k are allowed. Multi-depth controls also receive midpoint pulses, randomized quadrature debiasing, and sign-specific valid stopping.
strong_comparator_policy.literature_anchor_pending_detail: Kimmel, Low and Yoder, Robust calibration of a universal single-qubit gate set via robust phase estimation, Phys.Rev.A92,062315(2015), arXiv1502.02677. Its noiseless/robust phase-estimation rates must not be applied unmodified to depth-dependent dephasing. This file does not claim to reproduce that algorithm.
strong_comparator_policy.executable_mathematical_policy: At fixedk draw independent fairS, observeY, setZ=S(2Y-1). UpdateM_plus*=1+bZ andM_minus*=1-bZ. Starting from1, stop at the first value>=200: plus rejects the update, minus accepts it. If neither crosses by2^20 observations, abstain. Use(k,b)=(8,3/250) or(16,7/500). All constants are public and independent of the unknown model.

proofs.item: Exact nuisance-bias removal and sign safety
proofs.argument: P[Z=+1]=[P(Y=1|S=+1)+P(Y=0|S=-1)]/2=(1+mu_k)/2, mu_k=v exp(-gamma*k)sin(k*phi), independent ofa. Sincek<=16 and|phi|<=.02, sin(k*phi) has the sign ofphi and henceDelta. UnderDelta<=0, M_plus is a nonnegative supermartingale; underDelta>=0, M_minus is one. Ville gives each wrong-direction probability<=1/200. AtDelta=0 the union of both directions is<=1/100, satisfying the original1% requirement.

proofs.item: Uniform power with a finite cap and unknown gamma/visibility
proofs.argument: For |Delta|>=epsilon, |mu_k|=2|Delta|exp(-gamma(k-1))*sin(k|phi|)/sin(|phi|). On0<|phi|<=H withkH<pi/2, sin(k|phi|)>=k|phi|cos(kH) and sin(|phi|)<=|phi|. Hence|mu_k|>=mu_min=2epsilon*k exp(-gamma_max(k-1))cos(kH). The correct log process is a sum of iid increments a_b+atanh(b)Z, a_b=log(1-b^2)/2, with drift at leastd_min=a_b+mu_min*atanh(b)>0. Fornd_min>log200, Hoeffding gives P(no correct crossing byn)<=exp(-(nd_min-log200)^2/[2n atanh(b)^2]). Adding the wrong-direction bound1/200 gives the reported uniform correct-decision lower bound. No Monte Carlo or posterior credible interval is used.

proofs.item: Finite expected baseline cost including cap outcomes
proofs.argument: Consider the one-sided correct crossing time tau_plus without a cap. Positive bounded-increment drift and the preceding exponential tail make its expectation finite. Wald identity and overshoot at mostlog(1+b) yieldE[tau_plus]<=(log200+log(1+b))/d_actual. The actual two-sided capped time is no larger than tau_plus pathwise, so this upper bound includes all outcomes. Multiplying byk or(k+2.3) gives paid gate/device upper bounds. Mirrored negativephi cases have exactly the same demodulated stopping-time distribution.

proofs.item: All-depth information bound from the same physical noisy state
proofs.argument: Before readout, rho_phi,k=(I+r_k[cos(kphi)X+sin(kphi)Y])/2, r_k=exp(-gamma*k). Use the single legal nullphi=0 with the same unknown gamma and readout parameters. Direct2x2 spectral algebra gives D(rho_phi,k||rho_0,k)=r_k atanh(r_k)(1-cos(kphi)). Any allowed measurement and the same noisy readout have classical KL no larger by data processing. This is one common null across all depths; no depth-dependent nuisance null is silently substituted.

r atanh(r)=sum_{n>=0}r^(2n+2)/(2n+1). Withx=gamma*k and1-cos(kphi)<=(kphi)^2/2, D_k/k<=[phi^2/(2gamma)]x exp(-x)atanh(exp(-x)). Eachx exp(-(2n+2)x) has maximum1/[e(2n+2)]. Summing the resulting positive terms gives sum1/[(2n+1)(2n+2)]=log2. ThereforeD_k/k<=phi^2 log2/(2e gamma) for EVERY positive depth, with no small-phi approximation.

SimilarlyD_k<=[phi^2/(2gamma^2)]x^2 exp(-x)atanh(exp(-x)). The maximum ofx^2 exp(-(2n+2)x) is1/[e^2(n+1)^2]. The resulting sum is sum_{m>=1}1/[m^2(2m-1)]=4log2-pi^2/6, from1/[m^2(2m-1)]=4/(2m-1)-2/m-1/m^2. ThusD_k<=phi^2(4log2-pi^2/6)/(2e^2 gamma^2) at every depth.

proofs.item: Sequential finite-risk lower bounds, including abstention
proofs.argument: For any predictable sequence of allowed actions and any finite-budget decision, the chain rule bounds transcript KL byI_shot*E[N] and also byI_gate*E[G]. On the event of a correct beneficial acceptance or harmful rejection, its probability is>=.95 at the scored model and<=.01 at the common nullphi=0. Binary data processing therefore gives transcript KL>=kappa=kl(.95||.01), even with cap abstention. HenceE[N]>=kappa/I_shot, E[G]>=kappa/I_gate, andE[T]>=kappa(2.2/I_shot+1/I_gate). These bounds hold with arbitrary adaptive depth choices and all accessible nuisance-learning observations charged.

proofs.item: Exclusion relative to the strongest qualifying control
proofs.argument: For a proposed new verifier A meeting the same error and power obligations, C_A is at least the appropriate information lower bound. The strongest qualifying comparator cost C_best is at most the displayed feasible fixed-depth upper bound. ThusC_best/C_A<=C_control_upper/C_information_lower. The certified ratios below are all<3 at both mirrored score points. Since the mean-ratio geometric mean over these two points is also<3, this declared two-point model experiment cannot meet the original3x criterion, even if a stronger comparator is subsequently added.

maximum_possible_new_method_speedup_vs_s.threefold_target: Excluded for this declared family score pair by a finite-error information bound and a feasible same-resource comparator.

amplification_really_changes_the_depth1_.interpretation: Coherent repetition is a genuine resource improvement here: it supports>15x fewer shots and>3x modeled device-time saving against the restricted depth1 class. Both benefits are shared by existing multi-depth/Ramsey methods and cannot be advertised as FaultTune beating the strongest same-resource comparator.

decision: Do not launch a Monte Carlo campaign seeking3x vs equal-resource multi-depth controls on this narrow noisy-phase family. The phase-amplification mechanism is useful relative to depth1 but its gain is already accessible to simple qualified controls. To pursue3x, identify a task structure or resource that supplies information unavailable to all such equally equipped controls, and rederive the null/cost model.
claim_boundary: This is a concrete proposed model-family feasibility obstruction, pending independent review. It does not claim that all noisy phase-estimation tasks lack3x opportunities, does not modify the frozen acceptance benchmark, and is not a SOTA comparison or full RPE reproduction.
